title: Blest Are the Sons of Peace
description: Blest Are the Sons of Peace in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 133, part 2, headed “Communion of saints; or, Love and worship in a family”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Blest are the sons of peace, Whose hearts and hopes are one, Whose kind de-signs to serve and please Thro' all their ac-tions run.

lines: Blest are the sons of peace,
Whose hearts and hopes are one,
Whose kind designs to serve and please
Their songs of praise, their mingled vows
The oil thro' all his raiment spread,
Where joy like morning dew distils,
And all the air is love.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
